newsitem.title: USA: Texas jobless rate steady at 5.4 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Texas jobless rate steady at 5.4 pct in July.

text.p: Steady economic growth helped hold Texas' seasonally adjusted jobless rate at 5.4 percent in July, unchanged from June and down from 5.6 percent in July 1996, the Texas Workforce Commission said Tuesday.
Nationally, the July jobless rate was 4.8 percent, down from 5 percent in June and 5.4 percent in July of last year.
Texas' actual jobless rate in July, which includes seasonal jobs like student summer employment, dropped to 5.7 percent from 6.1 percent in June and 5.9 percent a year ago.
It was the lowest July actual jobless rate since the 5.5 percent level reported in 1981.
The commission said that four out of the seven months of this year have recorded the same 5.4 percent seasonally adjusted rate reported for July. February, March and April had slightly higher rates.
The July rate is also as low or lower than all but one of last year's monthly rates (December).
The commission said total non-agricultural wage and salary employment was up by 14,800 jobs in July, with service industries accounting for 97 percent of the growth.
With the exception of construction and government, all major sectors experienced job gains.
"The annual (economic) growth rate remained at 2.7 percent for the second month in a row," the commission said.
The agency said strong growth, led by Houston, Dallas, Fort Worth and Laredo, boosted employment in transporation, communications and public utilities by 4,600 jobs during July.
Most of the state's 27 metropolitan areas followed the state trend. Jobless rates fell in all but three areas, two showed increases and one remained unchanged.
Bryan-College Station had the state's lowest jobless rate at 2.5 percent in July. The McAllen-Edinburg-Mission area had the highest at 17.8 percent.
